desc: Derive and prove the reduction: answer = min over feasible levels x of |Y−x|+|Z−x|; feasibility monotone ⇒ x ∈ [1, x_max] where x_max = widest-path (maximin) bottleneck between the two blocks; closed form: |Y−Z| if x_max ≥ min(Y,Z) else Y+Z−2·x_max.

Design the connectivity structure: maximum spanning tree (Kruskal / descending vertex activation with DSU) reduces pairwise maximin bottleneck to min-edge-on-tree-path; replaces rollback/persistent DSU + parallel binary search plan (simpler, O((N+Q) log N)).

Design per-query evaluator: binary lifting with numpy-vectorized batch LCA over all queries (min edge on path), O(LOG) vector passes instead of per-query loops; memory-safe int32 tables (~36MB total).

Implement the complete program: fast numpy input parsing, DSU max-ST construction (descending activation, weight = F of later endpoint), iterative BFS for depth/parent, numpy binary-lifting tables, vectorized query answering, output.

Validate logic on hand-crafted cases (single cell H=W=1 with same-block queries, equal blocks, low-bottleneck detours, tall vs short neighbors) and complexity-test with max-size random grids (H=W=500, Q=2e5) to ensure runtime (~3–5s) and memory fit.

Cross-check against a brute-force Dijkstra over (block, floor) states on many small random grids to confirm the widest-path reduction and query formula, and run a max-size timing test (H=W=500, Q=2e5) to confirm runtime and memory fit.
